title: Judgment ablation on the perturbed mesh
question: Does a bounded judgment stage after deterministic validation change which proposals are committed, and at what cost in throughput and task progress?

hypothesis.statement: With the evidence-heuristic judge, proposals made on degraded evidence (observations older than half the staleness limit) are withheld instead of committed. Replaying the recorded judgments reproduces the judged condition exactly. No judge can cause an unsafe commit, because judgment is only consulted after validation passes.

conditions.description: Validation and policy only; judgment is not consulted.
Deterministic evidence-heuristic judge (offline stand-in, not a model).
Judgments recorded in mock_judgment, replayed for the same seed.
A judge that disagrees with a fixed third of valid proposals.
TypeSafe Jev over the network. Runs only with credentials and --allow-network.

prediction.detail: mean paired difference -2.79 (100 pairs); 95% CI of the paired difference [-2.94, -2.64] lies below 0

unexpected: Condition `jev` did not run: network access not permitted (pass --allow-network).
limitations: The mock judges are deterministic rules in this repository; they show what a judgment stage does to the pipeline, not how a language model would judge.
One scenario. Effects depend on how much stale evidence the scenario produces.
